questions.question: The French apéritif Kir is chilled white wine mixed with crème de cassis, a liqueur made from which fruit?
questions.note: It was popularised by Canon Félix Kir, Resistance hero and long-serving mayor of Dijon, to promote local produce.

questions.question: The Rosetta Stone was uncovered by French soldiers in Egypt in 1799 but is displayed today in which London museum?
questions.note: French troops found the stone near Rosetta in 1799, but it passed to Britain in 1801 and has been in the British Museum since 1802.

questions.question: These are the red-carpet steps of the world's most famous film festival, held each May on the French Riviera. What is the top prize awarded there called?
questions.imageAlt: A red carpet running up a broad flight of steps to a large festival hall
questions.imageCredit: Palais des Festivals, Cannes · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The Palme d'Or has been the Cannes Film Festival's highest award since 1955.

questions.question: What is the largest lake by surface area in Great Britain?
questions.note: Loch Lomond in Scotland, at roughly 71 km², is the largest lake by surface area in Great Britain (Loch Ness holds more water by volume).

questions.question: The word 'tennis' is generally thought to come from an Old French word called out by the server. Which word?
questions.note: 'Tenez' is the imperative of 'tenir' (to hold/take), reportedly shouted by the server in the medieval French game of jeu de paume.

questions.question: The English word 'avant-garde' was borrowed from French, where it literally meant which military formation?
questions.note: In medieval French an avant-garde was the body of soldiers sent ahead of the main army.

questions.question: In the French département numbering system, which two-digit number belongs to Paris?
questions.note: Paris carries the code 75, a survivor of the former Seine département, sitting oddly between Haute-Savoie (74) and Seine-Maritime (76).

questions.question: In the 1956 Suez Crisis, Britain and France sent forces to seize the Suez Canal after which Egyptian president nationalised it?
questions.note: Nasser nationalised the canal in July 1956, prompting a joint British-French-Israeli intervention that autumn.

questions.question: The Vendée Globe, the solo non-stop round-the-world yacht race, starts and finishes in which French Atlantic port town?
questions.note: First run in 1989, the race has always started and finished at Les Sables-d'Olonne in the Vendée.

questions.question: Which duchess is traditionally credited with introducing the English custom of afternoon tea in the 1840s?
questions.note: Anna, 7th Duchess of Bedford and a friend of Queen Victoria, took tea and cake to bridge the long gap before a fashionably late dinner.

questions.question: On French railways, what three words does the abbreviation TGV stand for?
questions.note: The TGV is France's high-speed train, in service since 1981.

questions.question: Which British director made the 1962 desert epic 'Lawrence of Arabia' and the 1957 film 'The Bridge on the River Kwai'?
questions.note: Lean directed 'The Bridge on the River Kwai' first, then reunited with producer Sam Spiegel for 'Lawrence of Arabia'.

questions.question: At which Thames-side meadow did King John put his seal to Magna Carta in 1215?
questions.note: John met the rebel barons and sealed the charter at Runnymede, a meadow on the Thames between Windsor and Staines.

questions.question: In Proust's 'In Search of Lost Time', the taste of which small shell-shaped sponge cake dipped in tea unlocks a flood of childhood memory?
questions.note: The scene from 'Swann's Way' (1913) gave rise to the phrase 'une madeleine de Proust' for a trigger of involuntary memory.

questions.question: In the 2010 film 'The King's Speech', which British monarch does Colin Firth play as he tries to overcome a stammer?
questions.note: George VI, known in his family as 'Bertie', worked with Australian speech therapist Lionel Logue, played by Geoffrey Rush.

questions.question: Which country has the larger total land area: France or the United Kingdom?
questions.note: France, at about 551,700 km², is more than twice the size of the United Kingdom's roughly 244,000 km².

questions.question: In which sport do England and Scotland compete each year for the Calcutta Cup, a trophy forged from melted-down Indian silver rupees?
questions.note: The cup was made from the silver of the disbanded Calcutta Rugby Football Club and first contested in 1879.

questions.question: In France, if you drop your clothes off at 'un pressing', what service are you using?
questions.note: 'Pressing' is a false friend: it looks English, but the English word for the shop is 'dry-cleaner's'.

questions.question: The sandwich takes its name from John Montagu, an 18th-century holder of which aristocratic title?
questions.note: A keen gambler, he is said to have called for beef between two slices of bread so he could keep playing at the gaming table.

questions.question: This monument, France's gift to the United States, was designed by which French sculptor?
questions.imageAlt: A giant green copper statue of a robed woman holding a torch aloft
questions.imageCredit: Statue of Liberty · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: Bartholdi designed the Statue of Liberty, while Gustave Eiffel engineered its internal iron framework.

questions.question: Snowdonia National Park in north Wales is now officially known by which Welsh name?
questions.note: Since 2022 the park has officially been called Eryri, its long-standing Welsh name, thought to mean 'highlands'.

questions.question: An 'apéritif' is an alcoholic drink traditionally served at which point of a meal?
questions.note: The word derives from Latin 'aperire', to open — the drink is meant to open the appetite.

questions.question: The trophy known as the Claret Jug is awarded to the winner of which golf championship?
questions.note: First awarded in 1872, the Claret Jug (officially the Golf Champion Trophy) is golf's oldest major prize.

questions.question: Which French director made the 1997 sci-fi film 'The Fifth Element' and the 1994 thriller 'Léon: The Professional'?
questions.note: Besson, associated with the 'Cinéma du look' movement, also directed 'Nikita' (1990) and 'The Big Blue' (1988).

questions.question: Which French king was executed by guillotine in Paris in January 1793 during the French Revolution?
questions.note: Louis XVI was guillotined on 21 January 1793 in the Place de la Révolution, now the Place de la Concorde.

questions.question: The cooking term 'sauté', used in both French and English kitchens, comes from a French verb meaning what?
questions.note: It reflects the way small pieces of food are tossed so they 'jump' in the hot pan.

questions.question: France's only Formula One world champion, nicknamed 'the Professor', won how many drivers' titles?
questions.note: Alain Prost took the championship in 1985, 1986, 1989 and 1993.

questions.question: The Isles of Scilly, an archipelago in the Atlantic off Land's End, form part of which English county?
questions.note: The Isles of Scilly lie about 40 km southwest of Land's End and are administered as part of Cornwall.

questions.question: Which English actress has lived in Paris since her teens and built a major second career in French-language cinema, in films such as 'Tell No One' and 'I've Loved You So Long'?
questions.note: The British star was made a Chevalier of France's Légion d'honneur in 2005 for her contribution to French culture.

questions.question: What is the single Europe-wide emergency telephone number that also works throughout France?
questions.note: 112 reaches the emergency services free of charge across the EU, including France.
